FirmHome.notBuilt: A firm-wide close status per client is still not built: close readiness is read one client at a time, on that client's Close tab. Statutory deadlines are not recorded yet, so nothing here reminds you of one. And organising work in batches across clients does not exist at this altitude — the portfolio counts Work per client and links into the list that owns it.

NeedsYou.accrualBillConflictPlanPaused: This plan is paused, so none of the remedies is available. Resume the plan, or reverse the accrual with a journal entry of its own.

FirmSetup.heading: Firm setup
FirmSetup.pageDescription: The facts this firm still has to state about itself. Answered facts are never asked again, and nothing here holds up the rest of the workspace.
FirmSetup.unavailable: The firm setup checklist could not be read.
FirmSetup.noPlan: This firm has no setup plan on record. That is unexpected — every firm gets one when it is created. Ask an operator to look into it before answering anything here.

denied.title: Firm setup is for administrators
denied.body: Firm setup records facts about the firm itself, so it is limited to administrators and owners. Everything else in the workspace is unaffected — your clients, Work and activity are open as usual.

progress.heading: Progress
progress.workspaceStaysOpen: Nothing on this list holds up the rest of the workspace. Clients, Work and activity stay open while it is unfinished.

notice.seeded: The checklist is ready. Facts that were already answered have been kept as they were.
notice.committed: Firm setup is complete. The confirmed facts stay correctable below.

notStarted.title: Firm setup has not started
notStarted.body: There are {count} facts to state about this firm. Start the checklist to see them; anything already answered elsewhere will be kept.

completed.title: Firm setup is complete
completed.body: Every required fact has been recorded or deliberately skipped. Confirmed facts remain correctable below.

seed.help: This adds only the questions that are missing. An answer already on this firm's plan is kept exactly as it was and is never asked again.
seed.againHelp: An answer you have already given makes another question apply to this firm. This adds only what is missing; everything already recorded is kept.

commit.heading: Finish setup
commit.ready: Every required fact has been recorded or skipped. Finishing marks the checklist complete; the facts stay correctable.
commit.notReady: Finishing becomes available once every required fact is recorded or deliberately skipped.

identity.heading: The firm's identity
identity.purpose: How the firm is registered. These stay on the setup record with their author; they are not recorded as knowledge this wave.

tax.heading: Tax and financial year

accounting.heading: Accounting policy
accounting.purpose: How the firm's own accounts are prepared. Three of these are recorded as firm defaults in the Knowledge register.

tips.heading: A few things worth knowing
tips.purpose: Optional reading, never a requirement. Reading or skipping one just gets it out of the way.

item.correctOnRegister: This fact is on the Knowledge register. Correct or withdraw it under “Facts confirmed in setup” below.

form.reachesRegister: Recorded as a firm default in Knowledge
form.draftHelp: What you type is kept on this device until you save it, including if a colleague changes the checklist while you are working.
form.stale: Somebody else changed this checklist while you were answering. It has been re-read and your typing has been kept — check the current answers above, then save again.
form.alreadyRecorded: This answer was already recorded — the earlier attempt reached the server after all. The checklist above has been re-read and shows what is on record; nothing was recorded twice.
form.alreadyLive: This fact is already on the Knowledge register. Correct it under "Facts confirmed in setup" below rather than answering it a second time.
form.denied: Your role changed while you were answering. Firm setup is limited to administrators and owners.
form.notFirmDefaultable: This fact cannot be set as a firm-wide default. It belongs to a particular client rather than to the firm, so it is recorded on this checklist and nowhere else.
form.clientEvidence: A firm-wide fact cannot cite a document that is filed under one client. State it from the firm's own records, or record it against that client instead.
form.failed: That did not reach the server. The checklist has been re-read — if your answer is already shown above it was recorded; otherwise pressing Save again sends the same request rather than answering twice.

constraint.choice: Choose one of the listed values.
constraint.month: Enter the month as a whole number from 1 to 12.

skip.title: Skip this fact
skip.description: Skipping records that you decided not to answer "{question}" now. It does not hold up finishing setup, and you can answer it later.
skip.reasonRequired: Say why this is being skipped — a skipped fact without a reason is indistinguishable from one nobody looked at.

facts.heading: Facts confirmed in setup
facts.purpose: These went to the same record Settings and Knowledge read. They apply across every client that has no exception of its own.
facts.empty: No firm-wide facts have been confirmed yet. Answering the reporting framework, accounting basis or default currency records one here.
facts.authorityDowngraded: The person who stated this is now a {role} and would not be able to state it today. The record stands until it is corrected or withdrawn.
facts.authorityRemoved: The person who stated this is no longer an active member of the firm. The record stands until it is corrected or withdrawn.
facts.legacyNotShadowed: A client that already holds its own recorded fact for this keeps it; this firm default never replaces one.
facts.notCorrectable: This revision has been superseded or withdrawn, so it can no longer be corrected.
facts.correctDescription: A correction is a new revision of "{question}". The current value stays readable in the record's history.
facts.withdrawDescription: Withdrawing "{question}" is final: it stops applying to every client, and the withdrawal keeps the value it retires so the history still says what was withdrawn.

problem.reasonRequired: A correction or a withdrawal needs its reason.
problem.noGrammar: This fact's question is no longer on the setup checklist, so its value cannot be edited here.
problem.choice: Choose one of the listed values.
problem.month: Enter the month as a whole number from 1 to 12.

roleOptions.viewer: Viewer — reads the books and changes nothing
roleOptions.bookkeeper: Bookkeeper — prepares and posts the day-to-day work
roleOptions.admin: Admin — manages people and invitations as well
roleOptions.owner: Owner — signs for the firm; a firm always keeps one

roster.heading: Everyone with access
roster.description: The roster is published to bookkeeper and above.
roster.empty: No roster rows are visible here.

invites.heading: Pending invites
invites.description: Invitations are published to admin and owner only, so this list reads empty below that rank.
invites.empty: No invitation rows are visible here.
invites.issuerLapsedNote: The person who sent this is no longer admin or owner here
invites.noResendNote: There is no resend and no seat limit. An invitation's link cannot be recovered once it is sent, so to give someone a fresh one, revoke the invitation below and invite them again — the old link stops working immediately.

inviteDialog.title: Invite someone to this firm
inviteDialog.description: ClaraBook emails them a single-use link. The address is how they will sign in, and it is how the invitation is checked when they accept.
inviteDialog.ceilingNote: You can invite someone at your own rank or below. The firm refuses anything higher.
inviteDialog.addressInvalid: This address was refused. Correct it and send again.

removeDialog.title: Remove {name} from this firm?
removeDialog.description: They lose access immediately and any agent credentials they hold for this firm are revoked. There is no undo verb: inviting them again creates a fresh membership.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke the invitation for {email}?
revokeDialog.description: The link stops working. Revoking is also how you free this address for a fresh invitation before the current one expires.

courier.title: The invitation was not sent
courier.reference: Reference {id} — quote it if you ask for help.
courier.no_session: You are not signed in any more. Sign in and try again.
courier.cross_origin: That request did not come from this app, so it was refused.
courier.invalid_request: The invitation form sent something this server could not read.
courier.unsupported_address: This invitation service can only send to plain-ASCII email addresses, so nothing was created.
courier.not_permitted: Only an admin or owner can issue an invitation. Nothing was created.
courier.mail_not_configured: This deployment has no invitation mail set up, so nothing was created. Ask whoever runs it to configure the mail transport.
courier.recipient_has_account: This address already has a ClaraBook account — ask them to sign in with it. Nothing was created.
courier.mail_unavailable: The invitation service could not be reached, so nothing was created. Try again in a moment.
courier.mail_failed: The invitation was created but the email did not go out, and its link cannot be recovered. Revoke it below and invite again.
courier.transport: The invitation server could not be reached.

ClientTax.body: Malaysia's SST and income-tax lifecycle for this client. Once a close seals, Clara drafts every rung — its statutory citation and her own reasoning included — and a professional reviews and signs. Nothing here files or posts on its own.

sst.heading: SST
sst.subheading: This client's SST turnover watch, and where registration and returns stand.
sst.notBuilt: Clara does not yet track this client's SST registration, its taxable periods or the SST-02 return. Record the registration status and number in the client's knowledge facts meanwhile, and file the return the way your firm files it today. What Clara does track is the turnover watch above: it tells you when this client is approaching or has crossed the registration threshold.

ClientClose.heading: Close
ClientClose.body: Open a fiscal year, pick one to view its close plan — gates, doors, and the receipt/segregation record — or manage the close-prep hold and future-method attestation below. Every figure is read live from the DB.

begin.title: Begin close — {label}
begin.description: clara.begin_close opens the run and evaluates every gate. It also FREEZES the year: while the run is in progress no approved entry may be posted, changed or reversed with a date inside the period — by you, by a colleague, or by Clara — and the database refuses each attempt with write_into_closed_period. Abandon puts the year back to open. Needs the close_and_attest capability.
begin.restartDescription: The last close run on this year was abandoned, so the year is open again. clara.begin_close opens a NEW run and re-evaluates every gate; the abandoned run stays on the record with its own reason. It freezes the year again: while the new run is in progress no approved entry may be posted, changed or reversed inside the period, by anyone, and the database refuses each attempt with write_into_closed_period. Needs the close_and_attest capability.

finalize.description: Finalizes the year: clara.finalize_close re-evaluates every gate inside one transaction and either writes the close receipt or refuses, naming the gate that stopped it.

seed.asOfHint: The date the opening balances are stated as at — normally the day before the first period you will keep.

source.headerKeyed: Keyed by a person of your firm · {n} line(s)
source.readDocumentHint: Reads the bound document into opening lines. Every figure is re-derived by the database; nothing is approved by this.

outcome.parsedBody: {n} line(s) were read from the bound document and recorded with their provenance.
outcome.noLinesBody: This document does not contain a trial balance we can read. Key the balances instead, or bind a different document.
outcome.allOrNothing: Nothing was recorded: one unreadable line forfeits the whole document, because a partial opening basis is worse than none.
outcome.unmappedAccounts: Not in this client’s chart of accounts: {accounts}. Create them on the Accounts tab, then read again.
outcome.rereadBody: These opening lines came from an earlier reading of this document. Reading it again is refused on purpose — a second reading is not a retry — so bring the lines onto the newest reading instead. Every figure is re-derived by the database, and nothing is approved by this.
outcome.refreshedBody: {n} line(s) were read from the new reading of the bound document, and {retired} line(s) from the reading it left behind were retired.
outcome.noRereadBody: These opening lines already come from the reading this document stands on — somebody, or another tab, refreshed them first. Nothing was changed. Open this basis again to see the lines as they stand.
outcome.staleReadingTitle: The document has been read again since this page loaded
outcome.staleReadingBody: The lines could not be brought onto the reading this page knew about, because it is no longer the one the document stands on. Nothing was changed. Open this basis again and refresh from the newest reading.
outcome.mixedReadingTitle: Those lines came from two readings
outcome.mixedReadingBody: Every line has to come from one reading of the document, so this was refused before anything moved. Nothing was changed. Open this basis again and refresh once more.
outcome.deniedBody: Reading an opening source is restricted to a bookkeeper or above of this firm.
outcome.notFoundBody: This opening basis is not available to you.
outcome.failedBody: The request did not complete ({kind}). Nothing was recorded.

keyed.resolutionBound: A keyed resolution is bound to this seed.
keyed.mintResolutionDescription: The human keyed door — always open. Every keyed opening item's provenance binds to this record.
keyed.addTargetDescription: One line at a time; exactly one of debit/credit must be positive.

fixedAsset.keyedResolutionRequired: Mint the keyed resolution first — an untied seed's fixed assets require it.

acquisition.noDocument: No source document — this acquisition was recorded from stated figures.

schedule.blockedByParticulars: No schedule yet — it is projected once the depreciation particulars are answered.

ledger.emptyBlockedByParticulars: No depreciation has been charged yet because this asset's depreciation particulars are still outstanding.

particulars.proposalHelp: A suggestion, not a decision. Change anything that is not right — what is recorded is what you confirm, under your name.

actions.completeDescription: This sets the depreciation method once — a later correction goes through Revise, which is prospective and leaves history charged so far intact.
actions.reviseDescription: Mints a new register row effective from the date below; the current row is superseded. Cannot take effect on or before a period already charged.

actions.changeClassHelp: What KIND of change this is. The register keeps it beside the revision.
actions.changeClassRestatementNote: A policy change or an error correction is a retrospective restatement — ticket #680 owns that lane, under #679's lock law. Only a prospective estimate change can be recorded here.
actions.changeReasonHelp: One sentence a reviewer can act on. It is stored with the revision.
actions.disposeDescription: Books the disposal entry — stub depreciation through the disposal month, cost/accumulated relief, proceeds and any gain or loss.
actions.proceedsAccountLabel: Proceeds account (leave blank if proceeds are RM0)
actions.costPortionHint: Leave blank to dispose the whole asset.
actions.disposalDraftOutstandingRow: A disposal is already drafted (entry {entryId}) — approve or withdraw it before raising another.

sweep.heading: Sweep runs
sweep.definition: A sweep is one unattended pass Clara makes over this firm's filings inside a single time window. It records how many entries it expected to draft, how many it drafted, how many it skipped and how many it refused, and the run closes when it is finalized. A sweep never approves anything: everything it drafts still comes to a person.

The door (clara.acknowledge_sweep_run) is live but needs a run id, and no surface in the product hands a person one: sweep runs cannot be listed, and the sweep-receipt message that was meant to carry the id is never produced by the agent runtime.

merge.roleThisSurvives: {name} survives — the other party merges into it

statement.label: Label

Plans.heading: Plans
Plans.body: Accounting schedules you have explicitly authorised for this client.
Plans.boundaryBody: A plan creates journal Work on its due dates. It never initiates a bank payment and never creates or cancels a direct debit mandate. There is no global switch that turns scheduling on or off — each plan carries the instruction that authorised it.
Plans.listBody: Each plan runs under the authority of the person who instructed it, and every due date rechecks that authority before any accounting work is created.
Plans.empty: No accounting plans authorised for this client yet.
Plans.notFound: That plan is not in this client's books.
Plans.detailBody: What this schedule posts, who authorised it, when it next runs and what every past due date produced.
Plans.createBody: Name the instruction that authorises it, the schedule it follows and the entry it posts.
Plans.reviseBody: A revision supersedes the current schedule and keeps it, along with every occurrence that already ran under it.
Plans.endedNoControls: This plan has ended. Create a new plan to schedule this work again.
Plans.previewUnavailable: The next occurrences could not be read.
Plans.previewEmpty: This schedule has no further occurrence in its effective window.
Plans.previewPausedTitle: Paused — these dates are not being admitted
Plans.previewPausedBody: The schedule below is still recorded, and no accounting work will be created on these dates until the plan is resumed. Work already admitted is unaffected.
Plans.historyEmpty: No due date of this plan has been reached yet.
Plans.basisDateNote: Each occurrence posts on its own due date; the date stored with this basis is a placeholder the schedule replaces.
Plans.pauseBody: No further due date will create accounting work until this plan is resumed.
Plans.pauseNotCancel: Pausing stops future occurrences only. Accounting work that has already been created keeps running and settles normally — cancel it on its own page if that is what you want.
Plans.resumeBody: Due dates at or before today that have not already run will be admitted on the next scan.
Plans.endBody: Ending is final: this plan can never be resumed or revised again. Create a new plan if the work is needed later. Accounting work already created is unaffected.
Plans.endReasonRequired: Say why this plan is ending — the record keeps it.
Plans.catchUpBody: A schedule does not authorise its own history. Name the period you want caught up; occurrences are created oldest first.
Plans.catchUpBounded: At most twelve occurrences are created per request. Run it again to continue.
Plans.catchUpFromRequired: Name the day the catch-up starts.
Plans.catchUpToRequired: Name the day the catch-up ends.
Plans.catchUpFromInvalid: That is not a calendar date.
Plans.catchUpToInvalid: That is not a calendar date.
Plans.catchUpToBeforeFrom: The end of the window cannot be before its start.
Plans.catchUpBeforeAuthority: This plan's authority starts later than that. A catch-up cannot reach back past it.
Plans.overlapTitle: Another plan already moves these accounts
Plans.overlapBody: The plan was created. Another live accounting plan of this client already posts to one or more of the same accounts ({templates}), so check that the two are not both intended to run.
Plans.purposeFrozen: A plan's purpose is recorded when it is authorised and does not change with a revision.
Plans.kindNote: A reversing journal posts its accrual on the due date and reverses it on the first of the following month. Depreciation and close schedules are not created here, and a prepayment amortisation is configured from its own posted prepayment under Prepayments.
Plans.authorityNote: Choose the accounting work that carries the instruction for this schedule. A saved preference, a calculation policy or a repeated bank debit cannot authorise a plan.
Plans.authorityEmpty: This client has no accounting work yet, so there is no instruction to authorise a plan with.
Plans.dayRuleLastDay: The last day of the month
Plans.dayOfMonthNote: 1 to {max}. For a month end, choose the last-day rule — it is exact in every month.
Plans.effectiveToNote: Leave this empty for an open-ended schedule.
Plans.timezoneNote: Due dates are calendar days in {timezone}.
Plans.accountsUnavailable: The chart of accounts could not be read, so account names are unavailable.
Plans.issueAuthorityRequired: Choose the instruction that authorises this plan.
Plans.issueEffectiveFromRequired: Name the day this plan's authority starts.
Plans.issueEffectiveFromInvalid: That is not a calendar date.
Plans.issueEffectiveFromBeforeAuthority: This plan was authorised from {date}. A revision cannot start earlier.
Plans.issuePeriodAlreadyCovered: This plan has already run through {date}. Changing the frequency from a date inside that period would post it a second time — start the new schedule after it.
Plans.issueEffectiveToInvalid: That is not a calendar date.
Plans.issueEffectiveToBeforeFrom: The authority cannot end before it starts.
Plans.issueReversalCollides: A monthly reversing plan cannot accrue on the 1st: its reversal would land on the next accrual's own day.
Plans.reviseIsCorrectionTitle: This plan's figures are stated on an accrual
Plans.reviseIsCorrectionBody: Revising the plan here would move what the ledger posts while the accrual's own record kept the old figures, and the two would then disagree. Correct the accrual instead: that records the new figures on both, and keeps the link between the row it replaces and the row that replaces it.
Plans.reviseUnavailableBody: An ended plan is final. Create a new plan if this work is needed again.

Accruals.heading: Accruals
Accruals.body: Costs this client has incurred in a period but not yet been invoiced for, accrued on a stated schedule and reversed in the following period.
Accruals.boundaryConfigTitle: Accepting an accrual records it; it does not post it
Accruals.boundaryConfigBody: Accepting this configuration records the accrual, its schedule and the accounting work for the current period, all together. The journal entry itself is posted by that work, in its own commit — so a receipt here is not yet an entry in the ledger. This page shows which of the two has happened.
Accruals.boundaryShapeTitle: An accrual is a schedule, not a period-fact adjustment
Accruals.boundaryShapeBody: An accrual accrues an amount on its due date and reverses it on the first of the following period. A periodic stock adjustment or a supplied payroll obligation records a movement this period's own facts establish — it has no schedule and no future occurrence, and it lives under Periodic adjustments.
Accruals.billConflictsHeading: Documents posted inside an accrued period
Accruals.billConflictsBody: A document hit this accrual's own profit-and-loss account inside the period it accrues — a bill on an expense accrual, an invoice or receipt on an accrued fee — while the reversal that would net them together has not yet been admitted. Choose reverse now (once the reversal is due) or skip the next occurrence — nothing is posted or reversed silently.
Accruals.listBody: Each accrual runs under the authority of the person who instructed it, and every due date rechecks that authority before any accounting work is created.
Accruals.empty: No accruals recorded for this client yet.
Accruals.occurrenceCount: {count, plural, =0 {No due dates reached yet} =1 {One due date reached} other {# due dates reached}}
Accruals.methodStatedAmount: The amount stated here, accrued in every period of the authority window
Accruals.createBody: State the amount, the accounts, the service period it belongs to, the authority behind it and the schedule it runs on.
Accruals.detailBody: Its particulars, the authority behind it, and every due date it has reached.
Accruals.detailNotFound: We could not find that accrual in this firm.
Accruals.factTermSource: Stated by a person; a period read off a document by a model is never recorded here.
Accruals.factMethod: How each period's amount is chosen
Accruals.authorityNote: An accrual cites an instruction this database already holds. A preference, a calculation policy or a remembered conversation cannot supply it.
Accruals.planNote: The accrual and reversal schedule this accrual rides.
Accruals.notPostedYet: Nothing has been posted for this accrual yet. The accounting work for the current period has been created and will post when it runs.
Accruals.noReversalYet: No reversal is due yet. A reversal is admitted only once its own period's accrual has posted an entry that is still live.
Accruals.reversalPending: A reversal is due on {due}. It has not been admitted yet.
Accruals.reversalBound: The reversal due on {due} reverses entry {entry}.
Accruals.noOccurrencesYet: No due date has been reached yet.
Accruals.scheduleLastDay: {frequency}, on the last day of the month
Accruals.purposeHint: In the firm's own words. It names the schedule everywhere it appears.
Accruals.authorityHint: Choose the accounting work that carries the instruction. The database resolves it; a preference or a remembered conversation cannot supply authority.
Accruals.authorityEmpty: This client has no accounting work yet, so there is no instruction to cite. Record the instruction first.
Accruals.termNote: The period the cost belongs to. State it yourself — a period read off a document by a model is not an anchored fact and is never recorded here. The schedule below runs inside it, so every entry posts within the period it names.
Accruals.fieldMethod: How each period's amount is chosen
Accruals.methodHint: The rule is recorded because the rule is performed. This one accrues the amount stated above in every period of the authority window. It selects a figure a person stated; it calculates none.
Accruals.methodHintStatedPeriodAmount: The rule is recorded because the rule is performed. This one accrues the amount stated below for each due date separately, and the total above is never used in its place. It selects figures a person stated; it calculates none.
Accruals.sideExpense: A cost incurred, not yet billed
Accruals.sideExpenseHint: The expense account is charged and a liability account carries the amount until the bill arrives.
Accruals.sideRevenueHint: An asset account carries the amount until the invoice is issued, and the revenue account is credited. Both are reversed on the first day of the next month, so the invoice and this estimate never both count.
Accruals.assetHint: A plain asset account, not a receivables control account: a control account reconciles to identified open items and an accrual has none. 1180 Accrued Income is the standard chart’s own.
Accruals.liabilityHint: A plain liability account, not a payables control account: a control account reconciles to identified open items and an accrual has none.
Accruals.accountsUnavailable: We could not read this client's chart of accounts. You can still type the codes; the database checks them when you submit.
Accruals.derivedLinesNote: These two lines follow from the amount and the accounts. They are shown as they will be posted and cannot be edited here.
Accruals.dayRuleLastDay: The last day of the month
Accruals.dayOfMonthNote: 1 to {max}. Use the last day of the month for a month end — it is exact in every month.
Accruals.effectiveToNote: On or before the last day of the service period: an accrual for a term that ends cannot run for ever.
Accruals.timezoneNote: Due dates are calendar days in Asia/Kuala_Lumpur.
Accruals.fieldInstruction: The instruction, in the client's own terms
Accruals.instructionHint: What was asked for, and where it is recorded. The record keeps it.
Accruals.memoHint: Defaults to what is being accrued.
Accruals.draftNotKept: This browser is not keeping your draft, so a reload will lose it. Everything you type still submits normally.
Accruals.overlapTitle: Another schedule already moves one of these accounts
Accruals.overlapBody: The accrual was recorded. Another live accounting plan of this client already moves one of these accounts: {templates}. Check that the same cost is not being recorded twice.
Accruals.deniedBody: Recording an accrual needs a bookkeeper role in this firm. Ask someone who has one.
Accruals.lostTitle: We did not get an answer
Accruals.lostBody: Your accrual may or may not have been recorded. Sending it again uses the same identity, so it can never create a second one.
Accruals.lostTwice: Still no answer. Nothing has been lost — open the accrual list to see whether it was recorded before trying again.
Accruals.issueAuthorityRequired: Choose the instruction that authorises this accrual.
Accruals.issueExpenseAccountRequired: Name the expense account this accrual charges.
Accruals.issueLiabilityAccountRequired: Name the liability account it accrues into.
Accruals.issueAccountUnknown: This client has no active account with that code.
Accruals.issueAccountsNotDistinct: The expense and liability legs name one account. Name them separately.
Accruals.issueAmountRequired: State the amount accrued. An accrual of zero accrues nothing.
Accruals.issueSilentTerm: State the service period this cost belongs to.
Accruals.issueServicePeriodOrder: The service period cannot end before it starts.
Accruals.issueInstructionRequired: Record the instruction that authorises this accrual.
Accruals.issueEffectiveFromRequired: Say when this accrual's authority starts.
Accruals.issueEffectiveToBeforeFrom: The authority cannot end before it starts.
Accruals.issueEffectiveToRequired: Say when this accrual's authority ends. A cost belongs to a period that ends, so the schedule that accrues it ends too.
Accruals.issueWindowBeforeTerm: The authority cannot start before the service period it accrues for — the first entry would name a period it did not accrue.
Accruals.issueWindowAfterTerm: The authority cannot still be accruing after the service period ends.
Accruals.issueDayOfMonthRange: Choose a day between 1 and 28. Use the last day of the month for a month end.
Accruals.issueDayOfMonthAbsent: A last-day-of-month schedule carries no day number.
Accruals.issueReversalCollides: A monthly accrual on the 1st would have its reversal land on the next accrual's own day. Accrue on the month end, or on a day between 2 and 28.
Accruals.issueScheduleYieldsNone: This schedule never reaches an accrual date inside the authority window, so nothing would ever post. Choose a day that falls inside the service period.
Accruals.correctBody: Restate the amount, either account, the service period, the instruction or the memo. The schedule and the authority window do not move — the correction applies from the next due date, and every due date already reached is unchanged.
Accruals.correctionFrozenNote: The purpose, the authority and the schedule do not change here. The service period below must still sit inside the authority window shown above.
Accruals.alreadyCorrectedTitle: This accrual has already been corrected
Accruals.alreadyCorrectedBody: A correction supersedes exactly once. Open the successor to correct it further.
Accruals.lineageNote: A correction supersedes the row it corrects. The superseded row is kept, unchanged apart from this pointer.
Accruals.methodStatedPeriodAmount: The amount stated for each period separately
Accruals.amountTotalHint: With an amount stated per period, this is the total for the whole authority window. The stated periods below must add up to exactly this figure.
Accruals.periodAmountsHint: State what each due date accrues. Every period the schedule reaches must have an amount: a period left out posts nothing and is recorded as refused, and the total above is never used in its place.
Accruals.periodAmountsEmpty: No period has an amount yet. Add one for each due date the schedule reaches.
Accruals.issuePeriodAmountsRequired: State an amount for each period, or choose "The amount stated here, accrued in every period of the authority window" instead.
Accruals.issuePeriodDueDateRequired: Choose the due date this amount is for.
Accruals.issuePeriodAmountRequired: State the amount for this period. A period of zero accrues nothing.
Accruals.issuePeriodAmountDuplicate: Two periods name the same due date. State one amount for each.
Accruals.issuePeriodAmountsUnbalanced: The stated periods do not add up to the total accrued over the window.
Accruals.issuePeriodRemainderMisplaced: An even split leaves a remainder. Put it in the final period.
Accruals.issuePeriodAmountMissing: A period the schedule reaches has no amount. Add one for every due date.
Accruals.issuePeriodAmountNotScheduled: A stated period is not a due date of this schedule. Choose one the schedule reaches.

DeferredRevenue.heading: Deferred revenue
DeferredRevenue.body: Customer advances this client has taken, and the revenue each one recognises month by month.
DeferredRevenue.boundaryBody: A recognition schedule creates journal Work on each period's month end. It never issues an invoice, never touches MyInvois and never asks a customer for money — the advance was received and posted before any of this, which is what makes it deferred.
DeferredRevenue.configurationTitle: An accepted schedule is not a posted period
DeferredRevenue.configurationBody: Configuring a schedule records what will be recognised and when. Nothing is posted until each period's own due date creates accounting work and that work commits — the list shows how many periods have actually reached the books.
DeferredRevenue.taxTitle: Service tax is never recognised as revenue
DeferredRevenue.taxBody: Output tax charged on an advance is owed to the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, not earned from the customer. A recognition schedule moves the revenue leg only: an SST output line on the same receipt is left exactly where the invoice put it, and it is not a candidate for the deferred-revenue leg at all.
DeferredRevenue.attentionBody: A period that recognised nothing, and an advance that has posted with no schedule recognising it. Neither is visible anywhere else.
DeferredRevenue.attentionEmpty: Nothing is waiting: every live schedule recognised its last period, and every advance received has one.
DeferredRevenue.attentionTruncated: Showing the {shown, number} most recent. There are more than this — clear some, then reload to see the rest.
DeferredRevenue.attentionRefusingAdmission: Refused before any work was created, on {date}.
DeferredRevenue.attentionRefusingPosting: Work was created on {date} and the books refused it.
DeferredRevenue.attentionUnrecognisedBody: Received on {date} into a deferred-revenue account, with no schedule recognising it.
DeferredRevenue.attentionNeedsTerm: The invoice behind it states no service period yet. A person records that first — Clara never supplies one.
DeferredRevenue.attentionNeedsStatedTerm: It binds no document, so a person states the service period it covers. Clara may ask; she never answers.
DeferredRevenue.attentionReadyToRecognise: Its service period is recorded, so a schedule can be configured now.
DeferredRevenue.listBody: Each schedule runs under the authority of the person who configured it, and every period rechecks that authority before any accounting work is created.
DeferredRevenue.empty: No advance is being recognised for this client yet.
DeferredRevenue.stale: Showing the last reading; the newest could not be read.
DeferredRevenue.notFound: That recognition schedule is not in this client's books.
DeferredRevenue.detailBody: What each period recognises, the term it rode, and what every period actually produced.
DeferredRevenue.endedNoControls: This schedule has ended. Nothing more will be recognised against it, and a second schedule cannot simply be configured for the same receipt: the periods still to run are taken over only by a replacement derived from a corrected term.
DeferredRevenue.termSupersededBody: The service period this schedule was derived from has since been corrected. Nothing above has moved: a schedule is a derived record and its own allocation is never edited. The periods it has already recognised stand, and the balance they have not recognised is taken over by a replacement schedule derived from the corrected term.
DeferredRevenue.termStatedNote: This advance binds no document, so a named person stated the service period. The schedule is derived from that statement and behaves exactly like one derived from an invoice.
DeferredRevenue.termReasonWithheld: A named person stated this service period and recorded why. Who stated it and their stated reason are visible to bookkeepers and above.
DeferredRevenue.allocationBody: Derived from the advance's own deferred-revenue leg and the term its carrier states, exact to the cent, with the remainder wholly in the final period. It is a preview of what each period posts, not something to edit here.
DeferredRevenue.allocationMismatch: The periods this read returned do not sum to the advance received. Nothing here has been adjusted — open the entry and the schedule record before acting on these figures.
DeferredRevenue.historyBody: Every due date this schedule reached, admitted or refused, with the entry and receipt it produced.
DeferredRevenue.historyEmpty: No period of this schedule has fallen due yet.
DeferredRevenue.createBody: Name the posted advance, the revenue account each period credits and why that account. The amount, the term and the schedule itself are derived — you do not type them.
DeferredRevenue.derivedNote: The periods, the amounts and the due dates come from the advance's own deferred-revenue leg and the service period its carrier states. Monthly, on each period's own month end, in {timezone}, on a straight line — the only pattern this estate offers.
DeferredRevenue.sourceNote: An approved entry that credits exactly one deferred-revenue account enrolled for this client. Service tax on the same receipt is never a candidate.
DeferredRevenue.sourceEmpty: This client has no posted advance waiting for a schedule.
DeferredRevenue.sourceNeedsTerm: The document behind the chosen advance states no service period yet, so no term can be derived. A person records it on the document first.
DeferredRevenue.sourceNeedsStatedTerm: A person states the service period for this advance: it binds no document, so there is nothing to read a term off. State it below and the schedule can be configured.
DeferredRevenue.fieldAuthority: The instruction that authorises this schedule
DeferredRevenue.authorityNote: Choose the Work that records the client's instruction. A schedule cites an instruction someone gave; it is never authorised by the advance it is about.
DeferredRevenue.authorityEmpty: This client has no recorded instruction to cite yet. Record the instruction as Work first, then configure the schedule.
DeferredRevenue.revenueNote: Where each period's recognition is credited. It must be an active income account on this client's chart.
DeferredRevenue.accountsUnavailable: The chart of accounts could not be read, so account names are unavailable.
DeferredRevenue.revenueBasisNote: Required. A classification with no recorded grounds is refused rather than saved unexplained.
DeferredRevenue.purposeNote: What this schedule is for, in your own words. It names the plan.
DeferredRevenue.issueSourceRequired: Choose the advance this schedule recognises.
DeferredRevenue.issueAuthorityRequired: Choose the instruction this schedule cites.
DeferredRevenue.issueAccountRequired: Name the revenue account each period credits.
DeferredRevenue.issueAccountUnknown: This client's chart holds no such account.
DeferredRevenue.issueBasisRequired: Say why that revenue account before saving the classification.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_deferred_revenue_source_unfit: That advance is not one this lane can recognise.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_deferred_revenue_term_underivabl: No service period stands for that advance, so no schedule can be derived from it.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_revenue_target_ineligible: That revenue account cannot carry a recognition.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_revenue_target_underivable: The revenue account or its stated grounds are missing.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_deferred_revenue_amount_below_pe: The advance is too small to divide over that many months without a period recognising nothing.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_deferred_revenue_schedule_exists: This advance is already recognised by an existing schedule.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_revenue_recognition_schedule_not: That recognition schedule is not in this client's books.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_revenue_recognition_period_line_: This schedule has no period ending on that due date.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_recognition_pattern_unsupported: This estate recognises deferred revenue on a straight line over whole calendar months. Usage-based and milestone patterns need a measure of progress it does not record.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_client_not_found: That client is not in your firm.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_client_inactive: That client is not active, so no new schedule can be configured.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_authority_ref_unresolved: The instruction this schedule cites does not exist for this client.
DeferredRevenue.refusal_operation_in_flight: An identical request is already in flight. Wait for it to finish rather than sending a second one.
DeferredRevenue.refusalNotEnrolled: That advance's account is not enrolled as a deferred-revenue account for this client. Enrol it on the client's Registers page, then configure the schedule again.
DeferredRevenue.refusalPostedAnyway: The advance itself is still posted and the liability is still on the books. Your entries are kept — fix what the message names and configure it again.
DeferredRevenue.overlapTitle: Another plan already moves these accounts
DeferredRevenue.overlapBody: The schedule was configured. Another live accounting plan of this client already posts to one or more of the same accounts ({templates}), so check that the two are not both intended to run.
DeferredRevenue.rosterEmptyTitle: No deferred-revenue account is enrolled for this client
DeferredRevenue.rosterEmptyBody: Only an account the firm has enrolled as holding customer advances can be recognised into revenue. Until one is enrolled, nothing here can be configured — including advances that are already posted.
DeferredRevenue.stateTermBody: The first and last day the advance covers, and why you know that. Both dates and the reason are recorded against your name and can only be corrected by superseding them. Superseding a term never moves a schedule already running on it: the months it has recognised stand, and the balance is taken over by a replacement derived from the corrected term. Get the dates right before you configure.
DeferredRevenue.stateTermRefusalTitle: The service period was not recorded
DeferredRevenue.stateTermIssueDates: Give both the first and the last day the advance covers.
DeferredRevenue.stateTermIssueOrder: The last day covered falls on or after the first.
DeferredRevenue.stateTermIssueReason: Say why that period before recording it.

Prepayments.heading: Prepayments
Prepayments.body: Prepayments this client has recognised, and the amortisation each one runs on.
Prepayments.boundaryBody: A prepayment schedule creates journal Work on each period's month end. It never initiates a bank payment and never creates or cancels a direct debit mandate — it amortises a prepayment that has ALREADY been paid and posted.
Prepayments.configurationTitle: An accepted schedule is not a posted period
Prepayments.configurationBody: Configuring a schedule records what will be charged and when. Nothing is posted until each period's own due date creates accounting work and that work commits — the list shows how many periods have actually reached the books.
Prepayments.attentionBody: A period that charged nothing, and a prepayment that has posted with no schedule tracking it. Neither is visible anywhere else.
Prepayments.attentionEmpty: Nothing is waiting: every live schedule charged its last period, and every recognised prepayment has one.
Prepayments.attentionTruncated: Showing the {shown, number} most recent. There are more than this — clear some, then reload to see the rest.
Prepayments.attentionRefusingAdmission: Refused before any work was created, on {date}.
Prepayments.attentionRefusingPosting: Work was created on {date} and the books refused it.
Prepayments.attentionUnscheduledBody: Recognised on {date} against a prepaid account, with no schedule amortising it.
Prepayments.attentionNeedsTerm: The document behind it states no service period yet. A person records that first — Clara never supplies one.
Prepayments.attentionReadyToSchedule: Its document states a service period, so a schedule can be configured now.
Prepayments.listBody: Each schedule runs under the authority of the person who configured it, and every period rechecks that authority before any accounting work is created.
Prepayments.empty: No prepayment is being amortised for this client yet.
Prepayments.stale: Showing the last reading; the newest could not be read.
Prepayments.notFound: That amortisation schedule is not in this client's books.
Prepayments.detailBody: What each period charges, the term it was derived from, who authorised it, and what every period so far produced.
Prepayments.termSupersededBody: The service period this schedule was derived from has since been corrected on its document. Nothing above has moved: a schedule is a derived record and its own allocation is never edited. The periods it has already charged stand, and the balance they have not charged is taken over by a replacement schedule derived from the corrected term.
Prepayments.allocationBody: Derived from the recognition entry and the term the document states, exact to the cent, with the remainder wholly in the final period. It is a preview of what each period posts, not something to edit here.
Prepayments.allocationMismatch: The periods this read returned do not sum to the recognised amount. Nothing here has been adjusted — open the entry and the schedule record before acting on these figures.
Prepayments.historyBody: Every due date this schedule reached, admitted or refused, with the entry and receipt it produced.
Prepayments.historyEmpty: No period of this schedule has fallen due yet.
Prepayments.explainAdmission: The period was refused before any accounting work was created, so nothing reached the books and nothing is running.
Prepayments.explainPosting: Accounting work was created and the books refused the posting, so no entry and no receipt exist for this period.
Prepayments.explainChoiceCatchUp: Ask for this period again, once the cause is fixed.
Prepayments.explainChoiceCatchUpNote: A catch-up names a window explicitly. It is the only way a period that already passed is admitted, and it never reaches back past {authority}.
Prepayments.explainChoiceLeave: Leave it. A period the firm does not want charged stays refused, and the record keeps why.
Prepayments.explainClosedPeriod: That period is closed. Reopen it, or agree the treatment for a later open period, before asking for this one again.
Prepayments.explainAuthority: The person who authorised this schedule is no longer an active member with a bookkeeper role. Restoring their membership is what lets this schedule post again: a plan's authority cannot be reassigned, and a second schedule for this recognition is only ever opened by correcting the term it was derived from.
Prepayments.explainEgress: The firm's accepted Terms and Data Processing Agreement are what authorise Clara to act on this client's books. Accept the current versions and ask for the period again.
Prepayments.explainPeriodLine: This due date falls outside the allocation this schedule was derived from. Nothing has been posted and nothing will be: the allocation is fixed when the schedule is configured. If the term itself was wrong, correcting it on record is what opens a replacement for the periods that have not been charged; if the term was right, raise the difference with the reviewer.
Prepayments.createBody: Name the posted prepayment, the expense account each period charges and why that account. The amount, the term and the schedule itself are derived — you do not type them.
Prepayments.derivedNote: The periods, the amounts and the due dates come from the recognition entry and the service period recorded on its document. Monthly, on each period's own month end, in {timezone}.
Prepayments.sourceNote: An approved entry that binds a document and debits exactly one asset account. Anything else is refused.
Prepayments.sourceEmpty: This client has no posted prepayment waiting for a schedule.
Prepayments.sourceNeedsTerm: The document behind the chosen prepayment states no service period yet, so no term can be derived. A person records it on the document first.
Prepayments.fieldAuthority: The instruction that authorises this schedule
Prepayments.authorityNote: Choose the Work that records the client's instruction. A schedule cites an instruction someone gave; it is never authorised by the prepayment it is about.
Prepayments.authorityEmpty: This client has no recorded instruction to cite yet. Record the instruction as Work first, then configure the schedule.
Prepayments.expenseNote: Where each period's charge is booked. It must be an active expense account on this client's chart.
Prepayments.expenseBasisNote: Required. A classification with no recorded grounds is refused rather than saved unexplained.
Prepayments.purposeNote: What this schedule is for, in your own words. It names the plan.
Prepayments.accountsUnavailable: The chart of accounts could not be read, so account names are unavailable.
Prepayments.issueSourceRequired: Choose the recognised prepayment this schedule amortises.
Prepayments.issueAuthorityRequired: Choose the instruction this schedule cites.
Prepayments.issueAccountRequired: Name the expense account each period charges.
Prepayments.issueAccountUnknown: This client's chart holds no such account.
Prepayments.issueBasisRequired: Say why that expense account before saving the classification.
Prepayments.refusalSourceUnfit: That entry cannot be amortised: a schedule amortises a POSTED entry that debits exactly one asset account.
Prepayments.refusalTermUnderivable: The document behind that entry states no service period, so there is no term to amortise over. A person records the service period on the document first.
Prepayments.refusalTargetIneligible: That account cannot carry an amortisation charge. Choose an active expense account from this client's chart.
Prepayments.refusalTargetUnderivable: The expense account needs its stated grounds before the classification is recorded.
Prepayments.refusalBelowGranularity: That term charges nothing in at least one period: the amount divided across the periods truncates to zero. A shorter term, or simply expensing it, is a judgement for you to make.
Prepayments.refusalScheduleExists: That prepayment already has an amortisation schedule.
Prepayments.refusalPeriodLineMissing: That due date falls outside the allocation this schedule was derived from.
Prepayments.refusalAuthorityUnresolved: The instruction this schedule cites does not exist for this client. Choose one of this client's own recorded instructions and try again.
Prepayments.refusalOperationInFlight: The same request is already in flight. Waiting for it rather than asking twice.
Prepayments.refusalPostedAnyway: The prepayment itself is still posted and still needs a schedule. Your entries are kept — fix what the message names and configure it again.
Prepayments.overlapTitle: Another plan already moves these accounts
Prepayments.overlapBody: The schedule was configured. Another live accounting plan of this client already posts to one or more of the same accounts ({templates}), so check that the two are not both intended to run.
Prepayments.endedNoControls: This schedule has ended. Nothing more will be charged against it, and a second schedule cannot simply be configured for the same prepayment: the periods still to run are taken over only by a replacement derived from a corrected term.
Prepayments.unknown: The database refused this and gave a reason this page does not recognise. Its own words are shown above.
Prepayments.termReasonWithheld: A named person stated this service period and recorded why. Who stated it and their stated reason are visible to bookkeepers and above.
Prepayments.termStatedNote: This prepayment binds no document, so a named person stated the service period. The schedule is derived from that statement and behaves exactly like one derived from a document.
Prepayments.attentionNeedsStatedTerm: This prepayment binds no document, so there is nothing to read a term off. A person states the service period — Clara never supplies one.
Prepayments.sourceNeedsStatedTerm: A person states the service period for this prepayment: it binds no document, so there is nothing to read a term off. State it below and the schedule can be configured.
Prepayments.stateTermBody: The first and last day the prepayment covers, and why you know that. Both dates and the reason are recorded against your name and can only be corrected by superseding them. Superseding a term never moves a schedule already running on it: the months it has charged stand, and the balance is taken over by a replacement derived from the corrected term. Get the dates right before you configure.
Prepayments.stateTermIssueDates: Give both the first and the last day the prepayment covers.
Prepayments.stateTermIssueOrder: The last day covered falls on or after the first.
Prepayments.stateTermIssueReason: Say why that period before recording it.
Prepayments.stateTermRefusalTitle: The service period was not recorded
Prepayments.rosterEmptyTitle: No prepayment account is enrolled for this client
Prepayments.rosterEmptyBody: Only an account the firm has enrolled as holding prepayments can be amortised. Until one is enrolled, nothing here can be configured — including prepayments that are already posted.
Prepayments.refusalNotEnrolled: That prepayment’s account is not enrolled as a prepayment account for this client. Enrol it on the client’s Registers page, then configure the schedule again.

PrepaymentAccounts.heading: Prepayment accounts
PrepaymentAccounts.subheading: Only an account enrolled here can be amortised. Enrolling is a judgement about this client's chart, so it is recorded with the reason a person gave.
PrepaymentAccounts.empty: No account is enrolled as a prepayment account for this client yet. Until one is, no prepayment here can be amortised.
PrepaymentAccounts.enrolTitle: Enrol an account as a prepayment account
PrepaymentAccounts.enrolDescription: The account must be one of this client's own active, non-control, non-bank accounts of the type the purpose requires — an asset for prepayments, a liability for customer advances — and must not already be reserved by the fixed-asset or staff-advance registers.
PrepaymentAccounts.purposeDeferredRevenue: Advances this client received from customers
PrepaymentAccounts.purposeHint: A prepayment is an asset released into expense; a customer's advance is a liability earned as revenue. The accounts offered below change with this choice, because the door admits a different type for each.
PrepaymentAccounts.reasonHint: One sentence. It is the whole audit trail a later reader has for this decision.
PrepaymentAccounts.reasonRequired: Say why before enrolling this account.
PrepaymentAccounts.retireDescription: This closes the account to NEW schedules. A schedule already running keeps posting to the end of its term, and nothing already on the books moves.

WorkRestate.body: If the instruction itself was wrong — a different date, a different amount, a different account — this answer cannot change it. The admitted basis is frozen. Say what it should be instead and Clara records a new Work, with this one cancelled and linked to it.
WorkRestate.label: What should the instruction say instead?
WorkRestate.placeholder: e.g. this was paid on 3 September, not 1 September
WorkRestate.acceptedBody: This Work was cancelled and the new one carries your revised instruction. Both are linked to each other.
WorkRestate.notRestatableTitle: This Work can no longer be restated
WorkRestate.notRestatableBody: It has already posted, already settled, or already has a successor. The row below is the database's own answer.
WorkRestate.invalidBody: The runtime refused the restated instruction. Nothing changed, and this Work is exactly as it was.
WorkRestate.deniedBody: Restating accounting work needs a bookkeeper role in this firm. Ask someone who has one.
WorkRestate.lostBody: The restatement may or may not have been recorded. This page re-reads the Work — that row is the answer, not this message.
WorkRestate.unavailableTitle: We could not reach the runtime
WorkRestate.unavailableBody: Nothing changed. Try again in a moment.

WorkCancel.dialogBody: Anything already recorded stays recorded; nothing new will start. If an operation has already been accepted it will finish, and you will see its receipt here.
WorkCancel.stoppingBody: An operation that was already accepted is finishing. This Work will show its final state once that is settled.
WorkCancel.cancelledSuperseded: The run reported {outcome} as it stopped.
WorkCancel.completedAfterCancelTitle: This Work completed before the cancellation reached it
WorkCancel.completedAfterCancelBody: The entry below was recorded and stays recorded. A cancel never reverses a posted entry — a correction is a separate, linked operation.
WorkCancel.alreadyTerminalBody: This Work had already finished when the request arrived. Its state below is the database's own.
WorkCancel.deniedBody: Cancelling accounting work needs a bookkeeper role in this firm. Ask someone who has one.
WorkCancel.notFoundTitle: We could not find this Work
WorkCancel.notFoundBody: It may belong to another firm, or it may have been addressed wrongly.
WorkCancel.conflictBody: The database refused the request in the state it found. The Work's own row below is the answer — read it, then decide.
WorkCancel.unavailableTitle: We could not reach the runtime
WorkCancel.unavailableBody: Nothing was cancelled. Try again in a moment.
WorkCancel.transientTitle: That did not go through — try again
WorkCancel.transientBody: Nothing changed. The database was busy with another change to this Work at the same moment, so the request never ran. Pressing again is the same decision, not a second one.
WorkCancel.lostBody: The cancellation may or may not have been recorded. This page re-reads the Work below — that row is the answer, not this message.
WorkCancel.takeOverHeading: This Work is waiting for someone who can finish it
WorkCancel.takeOverBody: The person who asked for it no longer holds the role needed to post it. A bookkeeper in this firm can take responsibility; the new attempt runs under their authority and records the same entry.
WorkCancel.takeOverConfirmBody: Clara interpreted this basis from a conversation rather than being typed the figures. Read it below before you take responsibility for posting it.
WorkCancel.takeOverConfirmAction: I have read the basis — take responsibility
WorkCancel.takeOverAcceptedTitle: You are responsible for this Work
WorkCancel.takeOverAcceptedBody: A new attempt is queued under your authority. The person who asked for it stays on the record.
WorkCancel.takeOverDeniedTitle: You cannot take responsibility for this Work
WorkCancel.takeOverDeniedBody: Taking responsibility for accounting work needs a bookkeeper role in this firm. Ask someone who has one.
WorkCancel.takeOverUnavailableTitle: We could not reach the runtime
WorkCancel.takeOverUnavailableBody: Nothing changed. Nobody was made responsible, and the Work is exactly as it was. Try again in a moment.
WorkCancel.takeOverLostBody: The handover may or may not have been recorded. This page re-reads the Work below — that row is the answer, not this message.
WorkCancel.notTakeableTitle: This Work is not available to take over
WorkCancel.notTakeableBody: Its state changed while you were looking at it. The row below is the database's own.
WorkCancel.stopReplyHint: Stops this reply. Work that has already been accepted keeps running — use Cancel Work to stop that.
WorkCancel.stopDenied: Could not stop this reply — it is still running. Stopping a reply needs a bookkeeper role in this firm.
WorkCancel.stopAlreadyFinished: Nothing was stopped — this reply had already finished. What is above is the whole of it.
WorkCancel.stopUnreachable: We could not reach the runtime, so nothing was stopped. The reply may still be running. Try again.
WorkCancel.stopRefused: Could not stop this reply. The database refused the request in the state it found, so the reply may still be running. Try again, or reload to see where the turn got to.
WorkCancel.stopReattachReading: This tab has gone back to reading it, so the rest of the reply appears below.
WorkCancel.runLostSight: Lost sight of this reply — reload to re-check. What is above is what reached this tab.

Operator.heading: Operator support
Operator.pageDescription: Registrations, payments and payment-provider problems across the whole ClaraBook estate — the admission work only BELCORT's operator firm can do.
Operator.notOperator: This destination is for BELCORT's own operator firm, at owner rank. Your account does not carry that authority, so no support data or action is offered here.
Operator.isolationBody: Registrations, payments and payment-provider problems for the whole ClaraBook estate. It does not open any firm's documents, ledger, Work or Knowledge, and it carries no client navigation — operator authority is admission support, not access to other firms' books.
Operator.rowCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 support case} other {# support cases}}
Operator.emptyFirstUse: Nothing needs an operator right now — no open registration, payment or provider problem.
Operator.emptyFiltered: No support case matches these filters.
Operator.deniedTitle: Operator support is not available to you
Operator.deniedBody: This read is for the operator firm's owner. If your role or firm changed while this page was open, that is what the database is reporting.
Operator.failedReadTitle: The support queue could not be read
Operator.failedReadBody: Nothing was loaded, so this is not an empty queue — it is a read that did not answer.
Operator.staleNote: Could not refresh — showing the last support queue that was read.
Operator.caseSubheading: The affected entity, its current state, and the action this estate actually supports.
Operator.caseNotFound: No support case is available at this address. An unknown case, a mismatched kind and a case you may not read all answer the same way, on purpose.

noAction.registration: No supported action for this state — this registration has already been decided.
noAction.payment: No supported action for this state. A paid registration is claimed by the applicant themselves; this estate has no operator-side action that opens a firm from a payment.
noAction.problem: No supported action for this state — this problem has already been resolved.

Operator.approveReceipt: Firm {firmId} was created, with onboarding plan {planId} opened.
Operator.rejectDescription: This request will not be re-opened. The applicant sees your reason on their own pending screen.
Operator.rejectReceipt: The registration for {firm} was rejected, with your reason recorded.
Operator.resolveDescription: Record what was done about this provider event. Resolving does not move any money or open any firm — it closes the operator's own question about the event.
Operator.resolveReceipt: Provider event {event} is recorded as resolved.
Operator.reasonPlaceholder: What is being decided, and why?
Operator.reasonTooLong: The reason must be {max} characters or fewer.

failureTitle.stale: This case moved while you were looking at it
failureTitle.notFound: This case is no longer available
failureTitle.providerUnavailable: The provider could not be reached

failureBody.denied: The database rechecked your authority when you acted, and refused. Nothing was changed.
failureBody.duplicate: The same operation identity was already used. The first outcome stands — re-reading the case shows it; acting again would not repeat the effect.
failureBody.stale: Someone or something else decided it first. The queue has been re-read; the current state is shown above.
failureBody.notFound: It was decided, resolved or withdrawn. Nothing was changed by this attempt.
failureBody.providerUnavailable: Nothing governed refused — the request did not get an answer. Retrying with the same operation identity is safe: it cannot repeat the effect.
failureBody.refused: The refusal is shown verbatim above, with the database's own code.

Operator.capacityUnavailable: The admission capacity could not be read.
Operator.capacityFull: Admission is closed (the limit is reached)
Operator.capacityLimitHint: Leave empty for unlimited. Zero closes admission entirely.
Operator.capacityLimitInvalid: Enter a whole number of firms, or leave it empty for unlimited.
Operator.capacityReceipt: Admission capacity is now {limit}, with {count} firms admitted.

IntakeBatch.heading: Source batch
IntakeBatch.uncountedCompletions: {n} finished without a receipt this read could date
IntakeBatch.waitingBasis: Waiting: {question} on an open question, {fact} awaiting a fact, {attribution} awaiting attribution, {capacity} awaiting the daily quota, {unfiled} not yet filed to a client.

residual.preIntakeRefusal: A file the daily quota turned away keeps its record and shows here as waiting for the quota, but none of its bytes were stored — upload it again after the reset. The upload list above carries the database's own message and remedy.

empty.firstUse: No sources have joined this batch yet. Files uploaded on this tab while the batch is open will appear here with their own state and their own link.
empty.noResults: No sources in this batch are {facet} right now. Other groups still have rows.

denied.title: You cannot read this batch
denied.body: Reading a source batch needs a bookkeeper role in this firm. Ask an owner or admin to change your role, then reload.

failed.title: This batch could not be read
failed.body: The read did not answer, so nothing is known about this batch right now — this is not an empty batch.

pollExhausted.title: No longer watching for changes
pollExhausted.body: Some sources are still moving, but this page has stopped checking. Press Refresh to read again.

stopping.title: Stopping this batch
stopping.body: Operations already admitted are finishing. {settled} have already been committed and their receipts are kept.

cancelBlocked.title: This batch cannot finish stopping
cancelBlocked.body: The person who stopped it is no longer an active member of this firm, so the remaining operations cannot be asked to stop under that decision. Any other bookkeeper, admin or owner of this firm can press Stop again to take the decision over. Restoring that person's membership, or stopping each remaining work item from its own page, also works.

cancelled.title: This batch was stopped
cancelled.body: No new operations were admitted after the decision. Everything that had already been committed kept its receipt.

capacity.title: Waiting for the daily document quota
capacity.reset: The firm's daily document allowance resets at {at} {zone}.
capacity.body: A source the quota turned away keeps its place on this board with the database's own reason, but nothing re-reads it on its own — upload it again after the reset.

cancel.title: Stop the batch “{label}”?
cancel.body: {n} operations are still running. Each will be asked to stop, one at a time.
cancel.stillArriving: {n} more files are still being taken in or read. They are not running yet, so they will be asked to stop as they arrive — this batch keeps stopping until they are all accounted for.
cancel.receiptsKept: Anything already committed keeps its receipt. Nothing that has posted is undone.

FirmSettings.heading: Firm settings
FirmSettings.identitySubheading: Who you are here, and where the firm's own details live.
FirmSettings.identityNote: The firm's registered name, registration number and address are recorded on Firm details and setup. They are not repeated here.
FirmSettings.legalSubheading: The agreements this firm is operating under, and who accepted them.
FirmSettings.legalNotAcceptedForFirm: Not yet accepted for this firm
FirmSettings.legalYourAcceptanceNone: You have not accepted this version
FirmSettings.legalDraftNote: This is a draft. It cannot be accepted, and nothing in Clara depends on it yet.
FirmSettings.legalNotLiveHeading: This firm's legal standing is not current
FirmSettings.legalNotLiveBody: Clara cannot use a model on any client's books until an owner of this firm accepts the current versions of both agreements.
FirmSettings.legalNotLivePromptBody: Please accept the current versions of both agreements. During the beta this does not stop Clara working on your clients' books — it will be required before the official launch.
FirmSettings.legalNotLiveOwnerHint: An owner of this firm must accept the current versions.
FirmSettings.legalNotLiveOwnerNamed: An owner of this firm must accept the current versions. The most recent acceptance on record was made by {name}.
FirmSettings.legalLive: An owner of this firm has accepted the current versions of both agreements.
FirmSettings.legalMaskedNote: Who accepted an agreement, and when, is shown to bookkeepers and above.
FirmSettings.acceptDialogDescription: You are accepting version {version} on behalf of this firm. Your name and the time are recorded.
FirmSettings.acceptDialogReplayed: Already accepted on {date}. Nothing was recorded twice.
FirmSettings.acceptDialogStaleHeading: This agreement changed while you were reading it
FirmSettings.acceptDialogStaleBody: A newer version is now current. Read it and accept that one instead — the version you were shown is no longer the one in force.
FirmSettings.acceptDialogUnavailable: This did not reach the database. Nothing was recorded, and trying again is safe.
FirmSettings.acceptDialogReadFailed: The agreement text could not be read, so there is nothing to accept yet.
FirmSettings.commercialSubheading: What this firm is on, and what the database holds about it.
FirmSettings.commercialPlanNone: No plan is current for this firm
FirmSettings.commercialPlanUnruled: Beta — no price has been set for this plan yet
FirmSettings.commercialPaymentNone: No payment is recorded for this firm
FirmSettings.commercialSubscriptionPresent: A subscription is attached to that payment
FirmSettings.commercialInvoicesUnavailable: Clara does not collect subscription invoices for your firm, so there is nothing to list or download here. This is about the firm's own subscription; a client's invoices live on that client's own pages.
FirmSettings.commercialSupport: Write to support about a commercial arrangement
FirmSettings.commercialDenied: Plan and payment are shown to admins and owners.
FirmSettings.capacitySubheading: The four processing caps this firm sets for itself.
FirmSettings.capacityNone: No per-firm processing caps are recorded for this firm. The processing lanes apply their own built-in limits.
FirmSettings.capacitySourceNote: An owner or admin of this firm sets these. Every change is receipted and recorded against the person who made it. Clara's own estate ceiling stands above whatever you set here.
FirmSettings.capacitySeatsNote: There is no per-firm seat count. Seats are accepted product direction with no delivery date.
FirmSettings.capacityEditHint: Whole numbers above zero. Change only what you mean to move — a field you leave alone keeps the cap it has. Clearing a field leaves that cap alone too.
FirmSettings.capacityFieldInvalid: Each cap is a whole number from 1 to 2,147,483,647. Clear a field to leave that cap as it is.
FirmSettings.capacityUnavailable: That change could not be sent, so nothing was saved. Try again.
FirmSettings.capacityReceipt: Saved. This firm now processes up to {docs} documents and {pages} pages a day, {ocr} documents at once and {witness} model readings at once.
FirmSettings.usageSubheading: What Clara's models were asked to do for this firm, by month.
FirmSettings.usageBadPeriod: That month could not be read, so the current month is shown instead.
FirmSettings.usageScopeFirmNote: Calls made for this firm's own work.
FirmSettings.usageScopePlatformNote: Calls Clara makes for everyone. They are shown because they are real spend; they are never added to your firm's figures.
FirmSettings.usageCurrencyNote: Provider price ({currency}), not your books. Nothing here is converted to ringgit and nothing here posts to a ledger.
FirmSettings.usageUnpriced: {count} calls in this period have no price on record, so they are counted but not priced.
FirmSettings.usageDropped: {count} rows for this period could not be read, so this table is incomplete. Try again, and tell support if it keeps happening.
FirmSettings.usageEmpty: No model calls in this period.
FirmSettings.usageSeparation: These are Clara's own model costs. They are not a client's figures and they never post to a ledger — a client's own numbers are on that client's pages.
FirmSettings.usageDenied: Model usage is shown to admins and owners.
